adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:49 — GET /admin/groups/:id/users` route removed with no redirect/alias, replaced by unrelated `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/members`; any external caller still hitting the old URL now 404s (though the old action was itself unimplemented in the prior controller, so real-world impact depends on undocumented usage)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in config/routes.rb replaces the prior `get "users"` nested route under `admin/groups` with `put "members"` and `delete "members"` (i.e., the old `/admin/groups/:group_id/users` endpoint is removed and there is no redirect/alias added). That is a breaking API/URL change for any callers still using the old path; however, the diff does not show that the old route had a corresponding implemented controller action (so it may have been unused), making this more of a compatibility concern than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — Public `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` response shape changed from a bare serialized array to `{members:[...], meta:{total,limit,offset}}`, and non-automatic groups (previously returning the full unpaginated member list) are now always paginated with a default limit of 50; any external client parsing a bare JSON array or expecting the complete list will break/silently truncate

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array, and unpaginated except for `automatic?`) to always returning `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and always applying `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50 (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). This is a breaking change for any caller expecting a JSON array and also changes behavior for non-automatic groups from full lists to a truncated first page. The frontend group members route/template is adjusted to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` (not `model`), but no pagination controls are added there, so the in-app group members page will now silently show only the first 50 members with no way to access the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — Admin `POST /admin/groups` payload shape changed from nested `group: {name, usernames, visible}` to flat top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`), with `usernames` no longer accepted at all on create; external callers still posting the old nested `group:` payload will silently fail to set name/visible, and any caller relying on setting initial usernames on create loses that capability

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Admin::GroupsController#create` from reading nested params (`params[:group][:name]`, `params[:group][:usernames]`, `params[:group][:visible]`) to flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`) and it no longer consumes `usernames` on create (membership is now handled by new `add_members` / `remove_member` endpoints). That is an API-breaking change for any existing client posting the old `group:` payload. However, the claim that old callers will “silently” fail isn’t strictly supported: with `params[:name]` missing, `group.name` becomes `''` and `group.save` will likely error and return `render_json_error group` rather than silently succeeding. Still, the compatibility break and loss of “initial usernames on create” capability in this endpoint are real concerns introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:29 — Admin `PUT /admin/groups/:id` payload shape changed from nested `group: {...}` to flat params, and no longer accepts `usernames` (membership changes moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` actions); external callers doing membership sync via the old single PUT with `group[usernames]` will silently no-op on membership

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the admin group update API to accept flat params (e.g., `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and removes handling of `params[:group]` and `payload[:usernames]` in `Admin::GroupsController#update` (old `update_put` logic deleted; new `update` ignores `usernames`). Membership changes are moved to new endpoints/actions `add_members`/`remove_member` with corresponding routes (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). Therefore, callers still sending the old nested payload (`group[usernames]`) will have those params ignored and the request can still return success if the group saves, effectively making membership updates a no-op. This is a backward-compatibility / API contract concern shown by the diff, not an internal correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:96 — remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) which deletes the join row immediately, then reports success/failure based on the unrelated group.save call, so an invalid/non-member user_id (delete is a no-op) still returns success_json even though nothing was removed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... success_json` (new code). It’s true that `delete` on the association can be a no-op (e.g., non-member `user_id`) and `group.save` doesn’t validate that anything was actually removed, so the endpoint can return `success_json` even when no membership changed. However, the prior behavior (removed in this diff) explicitly had tests that “succeeds silently when removing non-members”, and the new endpoint similarly appears designed to be idempotent/silent on missing members rather than erroring. So this is a valid review concern about misleading success criteria / redundant `save`, but not a clearly verifiable functional defect given the apparent intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers` early-return changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to bare `return ;` (stray space before semicolon), an inconsistent/sloppy style vs. the promise-returning contract implied by callers using `.then()

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` now does `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, so the method sometimes returns an AJAX promise and sometimes returns `undefined`. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded contract inconsistency vs. the prior always-promise behavior (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`). However, in this diff the visible callers were changed to no longer chain `.then()` (routes now just call `model.findMembers();`), so a runtime break from `.then()` usage isn’t directly verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",")` assumes `usernames` param is a String; a JSON array value raises an unrescued NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a clean error

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request supplies `usernames` as an Array (valid in JSON requests, e.g. `usernames: ["a","b"]`), `split` is undefined and will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 because there’s no rescue/validation here. This behavior is directly implied by the diff; the endpoint is new and lacks type handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public /groups/:group_id/members endpoint accepts an unbounded user-supplied `limit` param with no maximum cap, allowing a large result-set query (minor DoS/resource exhaustion) against any group the user can see

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum cap or clamping. This allows a user to request arbitrarily large limits on the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint for any visible group, potentially causing large DB queries and resource exhaustion. The previous code effectively constrained this (automatic groups defaulted to 200), but the new code removes any upper bound.
